body_text:
The Extreme Value Theorem (Weierstrass). If $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$
is continuous on a closed bounded interval, then $f$ is bounded and attains
both an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum on $[a, b]$:
$$ \exists \, x_{\min}, x_{\max} \in [a, b] \quad \text{such that} \quad f(x_{\min}) \leq f(x) \leq f(x_{\max}) \quad \forall x \in [a, b]. $$

*Proof Sketch*: Let $M = \sup\{f(x) : x \in [a, b]\} \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\}$.
Choose a sequence $(x_n)$ in $[a, b]$ such that $f(x_n) \to M$.
Since $[a, b]$ is bounded, by the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem $(x_n)$ has a
convergent subsequence $x_{n_k} \to x_{\max}$.
Since $[a, b]$ is closed, $x_{\max} \in [a, b]$.
By continuity of $f$, $f(x_{\max}) = \lim_{k \to \infty} f(x_{n_k}) = M$.
Since $f(x_{\max}) \in \mathbb{R}$, $M$ is finite and attained.
The minimum is attained symmetrically by considering $-f$.
